questions.question: What is the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?
questions.ideal_answer: Supervised learning algorithms are trained on labeled datasets where the input features and target labels are provided (e.g., classification, regression). Unsupervised learning algorithms work on unlabeled data to discover hidden patterns or groupings (e.g., clustering like K-Means, dimensionality reduction like PCA). questions.question: How do you handle missing data or imbalanced classes in a machine learning dataset?
questions.ideal_answer: For missing data, evaluate MCAR/MAR mechanisms; techniques include imputation (mean, median, KNN, MICE) or dropping rows/columns if missingness is excessive. For imbalanced classes, techniques include resampling (SMOTE, random over/undersampling), algorithm-level adjustments (class weights), and choosing appropriate metrics like F1-score or PR-AUC instead of standard accuracy.

Highlights why accuracy is misleading for imbalanced data

questions.question: Explain overfitting vs underfitting and how to prevent them.
questions.ideal_answer: Overfitting occurs when a model learns noise in training data, leading to high variance and poor test generalization. Prevent it with regularization (L1/L2), cross-validation, dropout, pruning, or getting more data. Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture patterns (high bias); prevent it by increasing model complexity, adding features, or training longer.
